scope: Theorem 8.3 (Exact repair by simultaneous switches) of the manuscript “Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree” (preprints/Deterministic-nonbipartite-Ramanujan-graphs-in-every-fixed-degree-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 178 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6d8ea4bb85aae750), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 74. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer d ≥ 3 and a constant C0 ≥ 1. Put q = d − 1, s = 2 √ q, a = 10−4 , e = n−2/3+a , Wb = n−2/3+100a , M = ⌈n1/3+10a ⌉. There are constants n0, k, depending only on d, C0, and a deterministic algorithm with the following property for n ≥ n0. Let G be a simple d-regular graph on n vertices. Let v2, . . . , vn be an orthonormal eigenbasis of AG on 1⊥, with eigenvalues λi, and put xσ i = s − σλi for σ ∈ {+1, −1}. Assume the following three properties. 1. Spectral confinement. For every i = 2, . . . , n and both signs, xσ i > −e/20. 2. Local spectral mass. For every vertex p, both signs, and every w ∈ [2e, 2d], X 2≤i≤n xσ i ≤w |vi(p)|2 ≤ C0w3/2 . 3. Typical edge blocks. For every pair wσ B ∈ [Wb, 2Wb] \ {xσ i : 2 ≤ i ≤ n}, define Rσ B = X 2≤i≤n xσ i ≥wσ B vivT i xσ i . All but a fraction C0n−.1 of the dn oriented edges (p, p′) satisfy the following bound for both signs: (Rσ B)pp (Rσ B)pp′ (Rσ B)p′p (Rσ B)p′p′ ! − 1 d − 2 √ q σ σ √ q ! max ≤ n−.024 . Here ∥·∥max is the largest absolute entry. The exceptional edge set may depend on the chosen pair of cutoffs. Given the adjacency list of G, the algorithm finds M vertex-disjoint switches, each deleting two edges and inserting two edges. In Od,C0 (nk) bit operations it outputs the adjacency list of a simple d-regular graph G′ on the same vertices such that −2 √ d − 1 < λi(G′ ) < 2 √ d − 1 (2 ≤ i ≤ n). In particular, G′ is connected and nonbipartite.
